text: The Toronto Local Appeal Body was created by City Council in March 2017 with an effective date of May 3, 2017. Toronto Local Appeal Body hearings began in late August 2017. The Toronto Local Appeal Body makes decisions on appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions under Sections 45 and 53 of the Planning Act. It replaced the function of the Ontario Municipal Board for hearing appeals of Committee of Adjustment matters where there are no related appeals at the Ontario Municipal Board. The Toronto Local Appeal Body is an independent quasi-judicial tribunal administered by the Court Services Division and maintains an arm's length relationship with City staff and City Council. The Toronto Local Appeal Body adopted Rules of Practice and Procedure (the "Rules") on May 3, 2017. City Council direct the City Manager and the City Solicitor to report to the April 5, 2018 Planning and Growth Management Committee Meeting with recommendations for changes to the Toronto Local Appeal Body Rules of Practice and Procedure.
